rotation_note: Unattended-run override: NO rotating subset. All 3 core keywords plus the entire politics pool (34 keywords, grouped into elections_public_opinion / geopolitics / policy_regulation) are working keywords today (37 total). Day-of-year 315 sets ORDER only: group lead rotates so no group leads twice in a row (geopolitics led 11-09, policy_regulation led 11-10, so elections_public_opinion leads today, then geopolitics, then policy_regulation); within each group the list starts at offset 315 % group_size in pool order (elections 9 -> 0: election deepfake first; geopolitics 10 -> 5: national AI strategy first; policy 15 -> 0: EU AI Act first). Queries were not checked with WebSearch (budget reserved for librarians); librarians should prefer outlet RSS/sitemap_news feeds over site: search for recency. Window: last brief was 2026-11-10, so items published 11-10 (after the prior harvest) through 11-11 are in scope. Context: Wednesday in Korea / Tuesday in the US and EU. 11-11 is Veterans Day (US federal holiday) so weight US Tuesday 11-10 agency releases and court dockets (BIS, FTC, FCC, DOJ, district courts) and expect few US federal releases dated 11-11; EU Commission/Council documents ahead of the informal European Council in Dublin on AI (Friday 11-13); Korean Wednesday items (과기정통부, 개인정보위, 선관위, 문체부, 교육부, 국회 예산 심사·과방위 법안소위); 수능 is Thursday 11-12 (AI-device cheating rules were covered 11-08/11-10 — only an actual incident with official action after 11-12 is new); Asia-Pacific releases (Japan, India, Singapore, Australia) and UK Parliament. Upcoming hooks (only official documents are new, previews are not): Dublin informal European Council on AI 11-13 (a draft declaration text or formal Council document is new; the 11-10 card covered 16 states missing AI Act authority deadlines and the delayed AI compute hubs); CCW 7th Review Conference on autonomous weapons in Geneva 11-16..20; House closed briefing with Nvidia's Jensen Huang 11-18; lame-duck Congress mid-November (NDAA AI provisions, chip-security bills); Meta's AI-scraping commercial terms take effect 11-20 (Norway and Brazil courts suspended them; UK CMA probe open); Delhi HC Kriti Sanon hearing 12-10. In scope: bills introduced/marked up, agency rules/bulletins, court rulings and filings, regulator enforcement, export-control actions, official post-election after-action reports on AI-enabled interference, platform takedown reports. OUT of scope: who won, seat counts, polling, horse-race analysis, commentary without a new document. Neutrality rule from sources.json applies: report decisions/filings/releases, attribute contested claims, no partisan framing.
